challenge.method: Check which object owns the state field and whether the registry’s reference to identity claim revision 1 leaves a gap for the claim under review at revision 2. Check whether the description applies to a downloadable distribution or whether the installation section establishes release support.
challenge.results: The state belongs directly to the matching entity. The earlier claim reference limits what the record can attest about claim history, but the historical assignment is readable directly from the entity fields. The registry contributes no independent corroboration of the upstream description. Together the two sources cover both clauses within their stated scopes. The opening explicitly describes the language. The installation section separately discusses binaries and source installation. It supplies context for distinguishing those artifacts from the language and establishes no release-support status.

limitations: Active is the Language Index classification of the Go language identity.
The identity is scoped to the Go project governed by the recorded publisher and does not classify any toolchain, distribution, or release support status.
The protected registry records the fact of the catalog assignment. It supplies no upstream language identity evidence and does not corroborate the README.
